html:
SMTO-SKL-0016 — This account isn't allowed to make that calendar change

GUID: 8828b308-47b9-54fa-9166-c525a4ac9407
Slug: google-calendar-calendar-read-only
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • Google refused the change because this account can only view that calendar, or because someone else organizes the event. Your calendar wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list your calendars. Check whether this calendar shows you can only view it. The list shows the access this account has on each calendar, so you can see why the edit was refused.
  2. If someone else invited you to the event, ask them to make the change. To just accept or decline, ask SMTO to reply to the invitation instead. Only the organizer can change an event's details, but every guest can reply to it.
  3. If the calendar belongs to someone else, ask its owner to give this account permission to make changes to events, then ask SMTO again. Once the account can edit that calendar, Google will accept the change.

What success looks like

  • SMTO makes the change and the updated event appears in Google Calendar.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the calendar owner or the person who manages SMTO. SMTO won't switch to another Google account for you; name the account yourself if a different one should make the change.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google returned 403 with reason readOnly or forbiddenForNonOrganizer: the selected account has only read access to the calendar, or the event is owned by another organizer.

What this means

  • Google returns HTTP 403 with readOnly or forbiddenForNonOrganizer reason. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns HTTP 403 with readOnly or forbiddenForNonOrganizer reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect calendar access role and organizer requirements for the specific operation.

How to fix it

  • Check the calendar's accessRole for the selected account (google_calendar.calendars or calendar_list_get) and the event's organizer. Use a calendar where the account is writer or owner, or have the owner grant edit access; do not switch accounts automatically.
  • Inspect the calendar access role and organizer. Select a calendar you can edit, or ask its owner to grant access; do not change accounts automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the calendar access role and organizer. Select a calendar you can edit, or ask its owner to grant access; do not change accounts automatically.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended authorized account has the required role or the operation is left unchanged.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
